mainTopic: Why רב הונא told the myrtle merchants to let the נכרים cut the הדסים: testing whether יאוש with שינוי רשות, שינוי מעשה, or שינוי השם makes a stolen item usable for a מצוה
overview: On the previous amud, רב הונא told the myrtle merchants (אוונכרי) not to cut הדסים themselves. The נכרים should cut the branches and hand them over. The נכרים may have seized the land from Jews, so the הדסים might be stolen, and using them would be a מצוה הבאה בעבירה. This amud finishes the reason. Land cannot be stolen, so a stolen item stops belonging to its owner only when יאוש happens while the נכרי holds it and the sale to the merchant then provides the שינוי רשות. The גמרא challenges this: the merchant's sale to customers is already a שינוי רשות. It answers that the advice is for the merchants' own הושענא, which they never sell. It then asks whether binding the לולב counts as a שינוי מעשה. It gives two answers: רב הונא holds a לולב does not need binding, and even if it did, a reversible change is not a change. Finally, the גמרא suggests acquiring through שינוי השם, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining רב הונא's advice: let the gentiles cut
steps.stepSummary: Land cannot be stolen. So the branches must be cut by the נכרים, so that the owners' יאוש happens while the branches are in the נכרים' hands, and then the sale to the merchants creates the שינוי רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And land cannot be stolen. Therefore, let them (the gentiles) cut it, so that the owners' despair happens while it is in their own hands, and the change of possession happens into your hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא wanted the נכרים, and not the Jewish merchants, to cut the הדסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land always stays with its true owner, so while the הדסים are attached to the ground they still belong to the Jewish owner. Once the נכרים cut them, they become movable stolen goods. The owner's יאוש, combined with the sale to the merchant as a שינוי רשות, removes the owner's rights. If the merchant cut them himself, the stolen item would come straight into his hands with no change of possession after the יאוש.

keyTerms.meaning: Land cannot be stolen; it always stays legally with its owner
Therefore
The owner gives up hope of getting the item back
A change of possession, meaning the item passes to a new person
Let them cut it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic rule for the whole passage: יאוש alone is not enough. It must be followed by a שינוי רשות (or a שינוי מעשה) for the stolen item to stop belonging to its owner.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of the explanation. The words 'they' (אינהו) mean the נכרים, and 'your hands' (בידייכו) means the merchants רב הונא was speaking to.

phrases.english: And land cannot be stolen.
phrases.notes: Even after the gentile seizes it, the land and what grows on it stay the Jew's property

phrases.english: Therefore, let them (the gentiles) cut it,
so that the owners' despair will be
while it is in their own hands (the gentiles'),
and the change of possession will be into your hands.
phrases.notes: The sale from the gentile to the merchant is the change of possession

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of רב הונא's instruction, which was given on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הדסים must be cut by the נכרים, so that יאוש happens in their hands and the sale to the merchant provides the שינוי רשות.

steps.title: Challenge: the sale to customers is already a change of possession
steps.stepSummary: Even if the merchants cut the branches themselves, the item is in their hands at the time of יאוש. When they sell to customers, that sale is the שינוי רשות. So why does it matter who cuts?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, even when the merchants cut them, let there be despair while in their hands, and the change of possession into our hands (the buyers').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's advice. It points out that the customers would get the הדסים through a change of possession anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge moves the change of possession one stage later: merchant to customer instead of נכרי to merchant. If that works, there is no need for the נכרים to do the cutting. רב הונא's instruction seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, either way
Merchants or retail sellers (here, sellers of הדסים)
Into our hands (the buyers')

phrases.english: Ultimately, even when the merchants cut them,
let there be the owners' despair while in their hands,
and the change of possession into our hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the need for the advice explained in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's insistence that the נכרים cut the הדסים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The merchant's sale to the customer already supplies a שינוי רשות after יאוש. So the customer receives a permitted item no matter who cut it.

steps.title: Answer: the advice is for the merchants' own bundles
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's advice was needed only for the הושענא the merchants keep for their own מצוה. No later sale will happen to those, so the only possible שינוי רשות is the purchase from the נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for the merchants' own bundles (הושענא).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. The advice is about the merchants' personal הדסים, not the ones they sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the bundles sold to customers, the challenge is correct: the sale provides the שינוי רשות. But a merchant using his own bundle never sells it. If he cut it himself, there would be no change of possession after the יאוש. That is why the נכרים must cut it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a specific case
A bundle of the מינים (here, the הדסים) used for the מצוה
Themselves

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's advice applies to the merchants' own הדסים. The ones they sell to others already pass through a שינוי רשות when sold.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
for the bundles of the merchants themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by limiting the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The advice seemed to cover all the הדסים the merchants handle, which made it unnecessary because of the later sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: The advice covers only the merchants' personal bundles, where no later שינוי רשות will take place.

steps.title: Challenge: binding the לולב should count as a physical change
steps.stepSummary: Even for the merchants' own bundles, binding the הדסים with the לולב should be a שינוי מעשה. That, together with יאוש, would let them acquire the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them acquire it through a change made by an action!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. There may be another way, besides a change of possession, for the merchant to own the הדסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like שינוי רשות, a שינוי מעשה (physically changing the item) after יאוש makes the item belong to the one who changed it. When the merchant binds the הדסים into the לולב bundle, that might be such a change. If so, he would own them and could cut them himself.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them acquire it
A physical change made to the item by an action

phrases.english: But let them acquire it through a change made by an action!
phrases.notes: Meaning the binding of the הדסים together with the לולב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 by suggesting a different way of acquiring
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the merchants' own bundles have no way to become theirs unless the נכרים cut them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Binding the לולב is a שינוי מעשה. Together with יאוש, that is enough to acquire the item, so רב הונא's advice would still be unnecessary.

steps.title: First answer: רב הונא holds a לולב does not need binding
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that לולב אין צריך אגד. Since the מינים do not have to be bound, no physical change happens to the הדסים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב הונא) holds that a לולב does not require binding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, according to רב הונא, nobody has to bind the הדסים at all. So there is no שינוי מעשה to rely on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the הדסים would be bound as part of the מצוה. רב הונא holds that one may simply hold the מינים together, unbound. Without binding, nothing changes the הדסים physically.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
A לולב does not need to be bound together with the other מינים

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָבַר לוּלָב אֵין צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד.
phrases.english: He holds that a lulav does not require binding.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר לוּלָב אֵין צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the factual assumption, based on רב הונא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הדסים are necessarily bound, which would create a שינוי מעשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא does not require binding, so no שינוי מעשה can be assumed.

steps.title: Second answer: binding is a reversible change
steps.stepSummary: Even if a לולב does need binding, binding is a שינוי החוזר לברייתו: untie it and the הדסים are just as before. A reversible change does not count as a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say a לולב requires binding, it is a change that reverts to its original state, and a change that reverts to its original state is not called a change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that works even according to those who require binding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To acquire an item through שינוי מעשה, the change must be permanent. Tying the הדסים does nothing to the branches themselves; once untied, they are exactly as they were. A change that can be undone is legally no change, so the merchant still needs the שינוי רשות from the נכרי.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want to say (even granting the other view)
A change that can go back to its original state
It is not considered a change

steps.whatToRemember: A שינוי מעשה acquires a stolen item only if it is permanent. A reversible change, like tying the לולב, does not count. So רב הונא's advice stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a שינוי החוזר לברייתו is not a change applies throughout the laws of stolen property, not just to לולב.

phrases.english: And if you want to say
that a lulav requires binding,
it is a change that reverts to its original state,
phrases.notes: Untying the bundle restores the myrtle exactly as it was

phrases.english: and a change that reverts to its original state
is not called a change.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר לוּלָב צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining what counts as a legal change
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any physical action on the item, such as binding, counts as a שינוי מעשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a permanent change counts. Binding can be undone, so it does not acquire the item.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither a later sale nor the binding of the לולב makes the merchants' own הדסים theirs, so the נכרים must do the cutting.

steps.title: Why not acquire through a change of name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the merchants should acquire the הדסים through שינוי השם. A plain אסא becomes something with a new name once it is used for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let them acquire it through a change of name, since at first it was called a myrtle branch, and now...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Even if binding is not a real change, the branch's name changes, and maybe that change lets the merchants own it. The sentence breaks off at 'and now', and the new name comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא checked two ways to acquire: שינוי רשות (Steps 2-3) and שינוי מעשה (Steps 4-6), and neither worked. Now it tries a third way, שינוי השם. If the item gets a new name, together with יאוש, that might count as enough of a change to acquire it. If this works, רב הונא's advice would again seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A change of name. The item is now called something different from what it was called before.
'And let them acquire it.' This wording signals a challenge.
A myrtle branch (the Aramaic word for הדס).
At first, originally
And now

steps.confusionAlert: שינוי השם (a change of name) is not the same as שינוי מעשה (a physical change). The branch itself does not change at all. Only what people call it changes.

phrases.english: And let them acquire it through a change of name,
phrases.notes: A new possible way for the merchants to acquire the branches.

phrases.english: since at first it was called a myrtle branch
phrases.notes: Before it was set aside for the מצוה, it was just an ordinary myrtle.

phrases.english: and now
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the new name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 ruled out binding as a שינוי מעשה because it can be undone. This step tries a different kind of change: a change of name.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's advice that the נכרי must cut the הדסים (as explained in Steps 3-6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a change of name together with יאוש lets someone acquire a stolen item, the merchants already own their own bundles through the name change. Then it should not matter who does the cutting.
